newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: SABIC, Mitsubishi to build methanol plan.
newsitem.headline: SABIC, Mitsubishi to build methanol plan.

text.p: Saudi Methanol Company (Ar-Razi) has signed an agreement with Mitsubishi Heavy Industries to build a fourth methanol plant at its facility in Jubail, Saudi Basic Industries Corp (SABIC) said on Tuesday.

"Saudi Methanol Company, a SABIC affiliate, has signed an agreement with Mitsubishi Heavy Industries to set up a fourth factory for chemical methanol within the framework of its complex at Jubail industrial city," a SABIC statement said.

Ar-Razi, which operates the world's biggest methanol complex with a current annual capacity of 1.4 million tonnes, is a 50-50 joint venture between SABIC and a consortium of Japanese companies led by Mitsubishi Gas Chemical Company.
Work on the fourth methanol plant would be completed in May 1999, SABIC's statement, released from Riyadh, said.
A third 850,000 tonnes a year methanol plant, due onstream in July would lift Ar-Razi's methanol capacity to 2.25 tonnes a year, rising to 3.10 tonnes with the fourth plant in 1999.
SABIC's total methanol capacity would reach 4.5 million tonnes when the fourth Ar-Razi unit was in operation.

Industrial giant SABIC is 70-percent owned by the Saudi government. The firm on Tuesday announced net profits for the first quarter of 1997 of 1.08 billion riyals, versus 1.15 billion in first quarter 1996.
